In [[mathematics]], '''geometric class field theory''' is an extension of [[class field theory]] to higher-dimensional geometrical objects: much the same way as class field theory describes the [[abelianization]] of the [[Galois group]] of a [[local field|local]] or [[global field]], geometric class field theory describes the abelianized [[fundamental group]] of higher dimensional [[scheme (mathematics)|schemes]] in terms of data related to [[algebraic cycle]]s.
